title: Stakeholder Synchronization Briefing + Decision Worksheet
content:
Purpose:
This one-page briefing + worksheet is designed for QBR leads to run a tight stakeholder sync (30–45m) where the primary goals are: align on renewal posture, capture decisions and next steps, and surface any executive escalation needed. Use this when you have multiple internal and customer stakeholders across renewal and product ownership.

Desired outcomes (pick 1–3):
- Clear renewal recommendation (green/amber/red) with rationale and required commitments
- Agreed list of prioritized risks and mitigation owners
- Executive ask defined (if any) and agreement on decision timeline

Meeting context:
- Typical cadence: 4–6 weeks before renewal window opens
- Attendees: CSM, AM (if different), Solutions Eng, Product PM (if feature gaps), Account Exec (for renewal/contracting visibility), Customer Success Manager Manager (for escalations)
- Prep time: 30–45 minutes reading for attendees; 60–90 minutes of internal prep for CSM + SE

Pre-Read Checklist (what to attach to invite):
- Latest usage + health snapshot (tokens/day, active seats, error rate, latency anomalies)
- Adoption highlights and blockers (top 3 wins, top 3 concerns)
- Open support or SRE incidents in last 90 days
- Last QBR notes and outstanding committed actions
- Draft renewal terms and suggested concession range (if applicable)

Agenda (45 minutes – tight script below):
1) Welcome and goal (2m) — CSM: "Quick goal: leave with a single recommendation for renewal posture and any exec asks."
2) Current state summary (6m) — CSM: 90s customer wins, 90s pains, quick metric chart highlight
3) Risks & mitigations (10m) — SE/PM: enumerate top 4 risks, proposed owner & timeline. Use the worksheet below to mark Likelihood x Impact.
4) Commercial posture & levers (8m) — AE/CSM: pricing expectations, outstanding procurement hurdles, required approvals.
5) Decision proposal (10m) — CSM presents recommended posture (Green / Monitor / At-risk) with 1-sentence rationale and required asks.
6) Commitments & next steps (5m) — capture owners, deadlines, and reporting cadence. Recap by CSM.

Facilitation script snippets (concise prompts):
- Opening: "We have 45 minutes to land a single, actionable recommendation and any exec asks. I’ll run the worksheet and we’ll call out owners for all mitigations."
- When conversation wanders: "Thanks — that’s useful, but to keep the decision tractable can we park that in the action list and focus on the top 3 risks?"
- To elicit decision: "Given the data and mitigations proposed, can we surface any objections that would prevent us from recommending [Green / Monitor / At-risk]?"
- If disagreement: "Let’s capture the disagreement and the specific piece of information that would move the position. Who owns getting that info and by when?"

Decision Worksheet (use in-meeting; fill one row per risk/ask):
Columns (fill live):
- Item ID (R1, R2, A1)
- Short title (1–6 words)
- Owner (name)
- Likelihood (Low / Medium / High)
- Impact (Low / Medium / High)
- Remediation/actions (1–2 bullets)
- Required resource or executive ask (Yes/No + short note)
- Target completion date
- Status at next checkpoint (Open / In progress / Done)

Risk triage guidance (quick rules of thumb):
- High Impact + High Likelihood = immediate exec ask candidate; include specific ask and target date
- High Impact + Medium/Low Likelihood = treat as prioritized mitigation but not necessarily exec escalation
- Low Impact = bundle and monitor; assign mitigation owner for visibility

Renewal Posture Taxonomy (pick one):
- Green: probable renewal (>80% probability). Signals: steady or growing usage, adoption milestones met, low critical bugs, procurement on track
- Monitor (Amber): open issues that materially affect decision; needs targeted mitigations and evidence within 2–6 weeks
- At-risk (Red): systemic gaps or financial/contract barriers that make renewal unlikely without significant changes or concessions

Scripted closing (CSM):
"Recap: We recommend [Green / Monitor / At-risk]. Rationale: [one sentence]. Executive ask (if any): [one sentence]. Owners and dates are recorded — I’ll share updated worksheet and a 7-day checkpoint invite. If anyone has objections to the posture, please flag now or we’ll treat non-response as agreement"

Follow-up cadence and templates:
- Within 24 hours: CSM shares completed worksheet and short recording or notes (1–2 bullets per row).
- 7-day checkpoint: quick status update (10–15m) to confirm mitigation progress.
- Final decision window: 2 weeks before renewal auto-renew/contract milestone, have explicit sign-off from AE + CS manager

Decision sign-off matrix (email template):
- Subject: Renewal posture sign-off — [Account name] — [date]
- Body: "We recommend [Green / Monitor / At-risk] for [Account]. Summary rationale: [2–3 bullets]. Exec asks: [if any]. Please reply with APPROVE / REQUEST MORE INFO / OBJECT. Sign-offs required: CSM, AE, CS Manager, (optional) Product PM. Deadline: [date]."

Helpful variants (pick depending on audience):
- Executive 15-minute: Condensed one-slide: top 3 metrics, single risk heatmap, recommendation, and single ask
- Technical deep-dive: Add 30–45 minutes after sync dedicated to SE + PM to walk playbook and remediation plan

Templates to copy into calendar invite body:
- Internal prep invite text (send to internal attendees 1 week prior):
  "Agenda: 1) goal 2) data summary 3) risk triage 4) commercial posture 5) decision. Please review attached usage snapshot and outstanding action list before the meeting. Bring any updates to your assigned mitigation items."

- Customer-facing QBR prep note (if meeting will have the customer present):
  "We’d like to align internally on renewal posture and outstanding items before the customer QBR. If you prefer to handle the renewal conversation in the customer meeting, flag it and we’ll coordinate language and asks."

Common pitfalls and how to avoid them:
- Pitfall: allowing meeting to become a technical deep-dive. Avoid by parking technical threads and assigning follow-ups.
- Pitfall: no clear owner for mitigations. Avoid by requiring owner + date for every item in the worksheet.
- Pitfall: not translating risk into a commercial ask. Avoid by always stating the specific executive resource or concession required if posture is negative.

Appendix: Quick checklist for CSM during prep (copy as a ticklist):
- [ ] Pull last 90-day usage + anomalous events
- [ ] Confirm decision window and any internal contract deadlines
- [ ] Draft recommended posture and 1-line rationale
- [ ] Identify top 4 risks and propose owners
- [ ] Prepare draft executive ask(s) with ask owner and consequence if not approved
- [ ] Attach prior commitments and current completion status

Notes / rough thoughts (working space):
- If procurement is the blocker, loop AE early and map procurement approvals by org
- Use the 7-day checkpoint as a forcing function to show progress to execs
- For accounts with multiple product lines, create a per-product mini-worksheet and roll up to a single posture

Document history: draft created by Aisha Patel; internal review with Marco, Chloe, David on 2025-01-22. Intended to replace ad hoc email threads and short-circuit last-minute escalations.
